claims.text: Dhampyrs, also called Shade Walkers, have not risen from Hell and carry no crimes to atone for, though they do have a dark side.
Their joss is more than luck: they are knots of coincidence who win at casinos and slip their pursuers, and those who study their half-dead nature can learn to focus it for superhuman feats.

title: Dhampyrs and the Courts
summary: Where half-damned children stand among the Kuei-jin.

claims.text: One dhampyr's estimate puts their number at around 900 across the Middle Kingdom, and many independent ones never meet another of their kind.

To join a wu, a dhampyr raised in a court needs a parent's leave to take part in the guanxi ceremony; an independent one must find a wu willing to perform it, and a wu made only of dhampyrs is possible.

title: Dhampyrs of the Golden Courts
summary: Half-damned children in akuma-ridden Southeast Asia.

claims.text: The whole region of the Golden Courts is thick with akuma, which shapes how its dhampyrs live; sons who survive to adulthood usually leave the jungles as soon as they can, and Singapore gives some refuge.

title: A Dhampyr's Life
summary: Sunlight and mortality for the half-damned.

claims.text: Dhampyrs are not immortal; they are born, live out their lives and in time die.
Most prefer the night sky to the sun, and a rare few blister and peel in its light.
